How do central banks use interest rates to control inflation?  

Central banks use interest rates as a tool to control inflation. When the economy is doing well and inflation is high, the central bank can raise interest rates in order to make borrowing more expensive and discourage spending. This reduces demand for goods and services, which helps to bring down prices and reduce inflation. Conversely, when the economy is doing poorly and inflation is low, the central bank can lower interest rates to make borrowing cheaper and encourage people to spend more.

Explain the concept of short selling in the stock market.  

Short selling is a trading strategy that allows investors to profit from falling prices in the stock market. It involves borrowing shares of a stock from another investor and selling them with the expectation that the price will decrease in the future. The investor then buys back the shares at the lower price and keeps the difference as their profit. This process is known as “closing the position”.

What is liquidity risk in financial markets?  ̶Liquidity risk is the risk that a market participant cannot buy or sell a security due to a lack of buyers or sellers. What is the difference between fiscal policy and monetary policy?  

Fiscal policy refers to the use of government spending and taxation to influence the economy. It involves the manipulation of taxes and spending in order to achieve certain economic goals such as reducing unemployment or inflation. Monetary policy, on the other hand, is the manipulation of interest rates and money supply by a central bank in order to achieve similar goals.
